label: Strength scales as L^2: the missing half of Galileo's square-cube argument (R7)
statement_en: A member of cross-section A made of material with breaking stress σ fails under axial load σ A. With isometric sections and the same material the breaking load scales as (L2/L1)^2, the static safety factor F_break/W equals σ k3/(k1 L) and falls as 1/L, stress W/A grows as L, and above L_max = σ k3/(k1 n) the member cannot carry n body weights.

hypotheses.name: scaling-strength-law#assumed-1
hypotheses.statement: Axial loading (bending has the same L^2 dependence with a different constant; not formalised).

hypotheses.name: scaling-strength-law#assumed-2
hypotheses.statement: Isometric load-bearing sections and the same material (constant σ): real animals thicken bones with size.

hypotheses.name: scaling-strength-law#assumed-3
hypotheses.statement: Nothing about any real giant: the checker rules only on a candidate that commits to isometry, the same material and a safety factor.

scope.basis: a theorem about a model: it applies wherever the design supplies the quantities it uses and accepts the hypotheses in scope.assumed
kernelChecked: F_break = σ A: with AreaLaw A and σ > 0, F_break(L2)/F_break(L1) = (L2/L1)^2 (breakLoad_ratio).

With CubeLaw W: F_break/W = σ k3/(k1 L) (safetyFactor_eq); the safety factor of the scaled body is the reference one divided by the length ratio (safetyFactor_scaled); stress W/A scales as L2/L1 (stress_ratio).
Above L_max = σ k3/(k1 n) the member cannot carry n body weights (cannot_carry).
